description: Issue B — after ASR, recognized text was pushed straight to the backend via the Crew API instead of appearing in the current chat's prompt input box for the user to edit and submit. The companion now lets ASR, Macro, K5, and board composer-editing navigation fall through the API-first route to the existing Kiro Crew live-composer controller. ASR/Macro text is appended at the caret without Enter; short Nav Left sends Backspace, long Nav Left repeats Ctrl+Backspace, long Nav Up sends Ctrl+A then Backspace, and K5 sends Enter to submit the visible edited text. K1-K3 stable-slot selection and optional Alt+N jump remain API-first. This FEAT is independent of FEAT-001 (disjoint implementation files).
steps: Read context.json and this file first. In companion/src-tauri/src/lib.rs, make route_board_via_crew_api return false for Inbound::Asr and Inbound::Macro so handle_frame reaches the existing kc_router, which maps them to ControlAction::Compose(text) and types into the focused Kiro Crew composer without Enter.

Let K5 fall through to the same live-composer controller, where Down/Long maps to Enter, so it submits the text after the user edits it. Keep K1-K3 Click stable-slot selection and optional Alt+N jump unchanged.
Let Nav Left short/long and Nav Up long fall through to the live-composer controller instead of editing crew_api_drafts, so board editing acts on the visible composer text.
Preserve empty-text and recognition-failure handling: kirocrew_control.rs route_input already drops empty Asr/Macro text; board-side ASR error/empty frames must not type anything.
Keep changes minimal and retain REST draft helpers only for compatibility; do not change the wire protocol or add a test suite.
acceptance_criteria: When the Crew API is connected, inbound `asr` and `macro` frames reach the existing ControlAction::Compose path, which types into the live Kiro Crew composer at the caret without Enter or automatic submission.
K5 Down/Long reaches the live-composer controller and injects Enter, submitting the visible text including user edits; K1-K3 API selection and optional jump remain unchanged.
Nav Left short/long and Nav Up long edit the live composer through Backspace, repeated Ctrl+Backspace, and Ctrl+A plus Backspace rather than modifying crew_api_drafts.
Companion cargo tests report 0 failed, firmware host tests report ALL TESTS PASSED, and npm run typecheck exits 0.
No wire-protocol change; shared/protocol/protocol.md remains untouched.
verification: cargo test --manifest-path companion/src-tauri/Cargo.toml -> expect 0 failed; this verifies the existing low-level Compose, Enter, and navigation mappings, but does not directly exercise the Windows-only route_board_via_crew_api fall-through decision.
Run the firmware host test script under WSL -> expect ALL TESTS PASSED.
cd companion; npm run typecheck -> expect exit 0.
End-to-end keystroke injection and the API-online fall-through require Windows, Kiro Crew, and board hardware; code review confirms those route_board_via_crew_api arms return false.
findings: ASR, Macro, K5, and composer-editing navigation now fall through route_board_via_crew_api to the existing live Kiro Crew composer controller. ASR/Macro append without Enter; K5 injects Enter; short Nav Left, long Nav Left, and long Nav Up edit the visible composer instead of crew_api_drafts. K1-K3 API selection and optional Alt+N jump are unchanged. Firmware host tests reported ALL TESTS PASSED, companion cargo tests reported 97 passed and 0 failed, and npm run typecheck exited 0. Existing unit tests cover the underlying Compose, Enter, and navigation mappings, but they do not directly instantiate the Windows-only API-first routing path. End-to-end injection and API-online routing still require Windows, Kiro Crew, and board hardware.
